record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.original_question: How can a larger set of experimental neutrino-nucleus data strengthen the interpolation between low-energy neutrino-nucleus models, such as Elementary Particle Theory, Effective Field Theories, the shell model, and the Random-Phase Approximation, and high-energy descriptions based on the Fermi Gas, while also improving extrapolations to neutron-rich nuclei of astrophysical interest that are not experimentally accessible?

evidence.quote: While the description of the low-energy regime exploits approaches like the Elementary Particle Theory, Effective Field Theories, or microscopic models, such as the shell model or the Random-Phase-Approximation, the Fermi Gas is the basis for the theoretical description in the high energy regime.

A larger ensemble of experimental data would put the interpolation, of the neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling between these two regimes, on even more solid grounds. This would also help the extrapolation to the case of neutron-rich nuclei of astrophysical interest that are not experimentally accessible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the theoretical modeling of neutrino-nucleus scattering across a wide range of incident neutrino energies. In the low-energy regime (roughly below a few tens of MeV), the cross sections are typically computed using approaches such as Elementary Particle Theory (treating the nucleus as a single object whose form factors are constrained by symmetries), Effective Field Theories of the strong and weak interactions, the nuclear shell model, and the Random-Phase Approximation (RPA), which builds correlated particle-hole excitations on top of a mean-field ground state. In the high-energy regime (roughly above a few hundred MeV), the standard description is the Relativistic Fermi Gas model, in which the target nucleus is treated as a degenerate gas of non-interacting nucleons with momenta filling a Fermi sphere.

Formulate and answer the following question. Given a (hypothetical) enlarged set of measured neutrino-nucleus cross sections σ(Eν, A, Z) on a variety of nuclei (A, Z) over a broad range of neutrino energies Eν spanning the transition region between the two regimes:

(a) Construct a quantitative interpolation scheme that smoothly matches the low-energy nuclear-structure-based predictions (EPT/EFT/shell model/RPA) to the high-energy Fermi-Gas predictions, in a way that is consistent with all the measured data and respects exact symmetry constraints (CVC, PCAC, current conservation, sum rules).

(b) Using this scheme, give controlled extrapolations of σ(Eν, A, Z) to neutron-rich nuclei of astrophysical relevance (e.g. those participating in r-process nucleosynthesis or core-collapse supernova environments) that are not currently accessible experimentally, together with rigorous theoretical uncertainty estimates.

Does there exist such an interpolation/extrapolation framework that is simultaneously consistent with all available data, respects the relevant nuclear and electroweak symmetries, and provides quantitatively reliable predictions for neutron-rich nuclei?
artifact.status_search_result: Neutrino-nucleus cross section modeling across the transition between low- and high-energy regimes remains an active and unresolved area, as documented in recent reviews (NuSTEC white papers, Snowmass reports). Tensions between data and models persist for medium-energy quasi-elastic and resonance regions, and extrapolations to neutron-rich nuclei for astrophysics still carry large theoretical uncertainties. No unified, fully validated framework currently exists.

status_evidence.title: NuSTEC White Paper: Status and Challenges of Neutrino–Nucleus Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews persistent discrepancies between data and models bridging low- and high-energy neutrino-nucleus interactions and identifies open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The interpolation between low- and high-energy regimes and extrapolation to exotic nuclei remain open challenges.

status_evidence.title: Snowmass Neutrino Frontier: Neutrino Interaction Cross Sections
status_evidence.snippet: Lists outstanding theoretical and experimental challenges in modeling neutrino-nucleus cross sections across energy regimes.
status_evidence.claim: A unified, experimentally validated framework spanning the transition region and supporting extrapolation to neutron-rich nuclei has not been established.
